title: Sidecar send-keys push occasionally delivers the [cam] line without submitting (missing Enter)
description:
OBSERVED (operator, recurring across multiple sessions/contexts): sidecar push lines ([cam] ...) sometimes land in the orchestrator pane's input as TEXT but are not submitted -- the message is produced but the terminating Enter is missing, so the line sits in the input awaiting a manual keystroke. Confirmed live this session: the '[cam] merge-watch timeout: PR #293 not yet merged after 240 polls' line was stalled un-submitted in the operator's input.

ROOT-CAUSE CLASS (known): tmux send-keys must deliver text + Enter in a SINGLE call. Two prior failure modes are documented: (a) Enter sent as a SEPARATE send-keys call becomes a newline in this TUI build instead of submitting (see memory tmux-drive-orchestrator-atomic-enter); (b) `-l` (literal) applied over the control token turns the string 'Enter' into literal text rather than a keypress, so nothing submits (CAM-55, sendkeys-literal-enter-gotcha, dispatch.ts:191 regression that broke all thin-proxies). That the symptom reappears across sessions suggests a remaining non-atomic send-keys path in the sidecar's push (likely multi-line message splitting or a retry path).

SCOPE: audit every send-keys call-site in the sidecar's push path (src/supervisor/*, dispatch) and guarantee atomic text+Enter delivery in one call -- never a standalone Enter, never `-l` over the control token. Pay special attention to multi-line [cam] messages and any retry/re-send path.

VERIFICATION: add an integration guard in the style of test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts that asserts REAL submission against a live tmux pane (the message actually reaches the shell/agent), not merely the argv shape -- argv-shape tests lie about tmux semantics (proven CAM-55).

Source: operator report 2026-07-19 during the CAM-357 ship (PR #293) recovery.

spec.scope: NARROWED RE-SPEC (supersedes the prior CAM-358 spec; see the parked branch cam/issue-358 for the abandoned attempt). Fix ONLY the inert post-send verification timing in sendKeysVerified (src/tmux/dispatch.ts), which is the actual cause of the operator's silently-lost [cam] pushes. Two changes: (1) wait a settle window via the injected sleepFn between the send-keys spawn and the verification capture, because capturing immediately reads the pre-send screen and misreports an undelivered payload as 'composer emptied', which breaks the retry loop on attempt 1; (2) raise the idle deadline from 5_000 ms to a realistic value as a named constant, because an orchestrator running a long tool call is routinely busy far longer than 5 s, which made the blind send-anyway path the common case. Evidence for both: cam-supervisor.log recorded 5 'did not go idle within 5000 ms; sending anyway' warnings while cam-worker-events.jsonl recorded ZERO push-undelivered events, i.e. the verify path never once fired across 5 blind sends. EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE: any change to the isComposerEmptied matching logic. The prior attempt tried to make it wrap-tolerant and burned two full review rounds producing successive CRITICALs (tail-join matched the transcript echo; a no-anchor fallback calibrated on the cat fixture's double-echo that the production Ink TUI does not exhibit; occurrence-counting over the full capture making the verdict scrollback-dependent; and a regex anchor forgeable by a '>' at a wrap-boundary column in the payload itself). Content-matching pane text is not a sound oracle and its redesign around pane geometry is tracked as a SEPARATE issue. Leave isComposerEmptied exactly as it is on main. Wrap-tolerance is latent, not the reported bug: the operator's pane is 138 columns and the lost payloads were 79-93 characters, so nothing wrapped.
acceptanceCriteria: sendKeysVerified waits a settle window via the injected sleepFn between the send-keys spawn and the verification capture; the delay is a named exported constant, not an inline literal.
The idle-wait deadline is a named constant well above 5000 ms; the send-anyway fallback still fires, still warns, and still never blocks indefinitely.
isComposerEmptied is byte-identical to its state on main: git diff main -- src/tmux/dispatch.ts shows no change inside that function.
The send-keys argv shape is unchanged: text and Enter in ONE call, never -l.
When retries are exhausted the push-undelivered event still fires with paneId and retriesExhausted.

A test proves the settle window is honored: with a capturePaneFn that returns the pre-send screen on the first read and the post-send screen after the settle, verification reports the correct verdict rather than the stale pre-send one.
bun test and bun run check:all are green with no existing assertion weakened or skipped.
gotchas: Do NOT touch isComposerEmptied. Making it wrap-tolerant is a separate tracked issue and every in-place attempt so far produced a CRITICAL regression.
Do NOT change the argv shape: text+Enter in one send-keys call, never -l (CAM-55 sendkeys-literal-enter-gotcha).
The settle must go through the INJECTED sleepFn so tests stay deterministic and fast; never a bare sleep.

The sidecar wires a different capture reader than the unit tests (host.ts:579-586 uses capture-pane -p -S - full scrollback; dispatch.ts:191-198 uses the visible-screen read). This narrowed scope does not require reconciling them, but do not introduce any new dependence on which reader is wired.
Bare sleeps are banned under test/integration/; use test/helpers/wait-for-condition.ts.

The parked branch cam/issue-358 (origin, 64e2a909) holds the abandoned wrap/anchor attempt plus the reviewer's real-tmux probe evidence. Do NOT branch from it or cherry-pick from it; start clean from main.
domainTerms: sendKeysVerified: the shared send+verify+retry helper in src/tmux/dispatch.ts, sole production emitter of [cam] lines.
settle window: the wait between send-keys and the verification capture that lets the receiving TUI read the keystrokes off its pty and re-render.
send-anyway path: the branch taken when waitForIdlePane times out; it sends into a possibly-busy composer.
push-undelivered: the structured event logged when the retry loop exhausts.
